result: In 45 Fukuda ME/CFS vs 27 controls, fMRI showed weaker connectivity within the brainstem (medulla to cuneiform nucleus) and from brainstem to hippocampus and intralaminar thalamus, only during a task and not at rest; weaker RAS connectivity tracked symptom severity.
reason: Group difference is task-only brainstem connectivity, not resting-state; fits the brainstem finding better (resting comparison was effectively null).

result: Replicating the Myhill mitochondrial energy score in neutrophils and PBMCs from 10 CFS/ME patients and 13 controls found no difference in any MES component (p>=0.059), and a 24 h processing delay significantly changed many parameters.
reason: Null result for blood-cell mitochondrial function; small sample but it also shows that processing delay is a confounder.

result: In 47 ME/CFS cases vs matched controls, 7-day PEM severity was linked to falling serum hypoxanthine, which correlated with a shifted glucose:lactate ratio (a suggested glycolytic anomaly), and to higher urinary methylhistidine, mannitol and acetate.
reason: Glucose:lactate shift fits the inferred fuel-use anomaly and adds a link to PEM severity; single cohort, inferential.

result: In 47 ME/CFS cases vs matched controls, 7-day PEM severity was linked to falling serum hypoxanthine, which correlated with a shifted glucose:lactate ratio, and to higher urinary methylhistidine, mannitol and acetate.
reason: No exercise challenge or CPET; it correlates self-reported PEM with resting samples. Already covered by the omics-energy-fuel-pdh link.

result: A systematic review of 18 CBT and GET RCTs rated their methodological quality as relatively low, with prominent bias affecting the main self-reported outcomes (fatigue, physical functioning, functional status).
reason: Supports the finding's criticism of the unblinded self-report outcomes across the trial literature; abstract gives no numbers.

result: Blinded testing of 50 patients and 50 controls at the Oxford neuroimmunology lab found any neuronal immunoreactivity in 8 patients vs 11 controls and specific antibodies in 1 vs 2; seropositive patients had shorter duration and more severe disease.
reason: Directly tests neural autoantibodies with gold-standard cell-based assays and finds no increased frequency.

result: Whole-cell patch-clamp of NK cells from 12 CFS/ME patients and 12 matched controls showed significantly smaller pregnenolone-sulfate- and nifedipine-evoked TRPM3 currents and reduced ononetin sensitivity in patients.
reason: New cohort, same measure and direction, but from the same group and tiny, consistent with the 'one group only' caveat.

result: Whole-cell patch-clamp of NK cells from 12 CFS/ME patients and 12 matched controls showed significantly smaller pregnenolone-sulfate- and nifedipine-evoked TRPM3 currents in patients.
reason: Functional channel study with no genotyping; belongs with the immune-trpm3 functional finding, not the genetics one.

result: In UK ME/CFS Biobank labs (272 ME/CFS, 136 controls), serum CK was lower in severe ME/CFS (median 54 U/L) than in controls (101.5) and non-severe cases (84), and this held after adjusting for sex, age, BMI, muscle mass, duration and activity (OR 0.05 vs controls).
reason: Same muscle marker (CK) is low in blood; adds a severity gradient and an adjustment for muscle mass and activity, which the finding could not address.

result: Of 784 young people (mean age 14.6) followed a mean 8 years after onset (81.8% response), 38% reported recovery by 5 years and 68% by 10 years (mean illness duration 5 years); 5% remained very unwell and 20% significantly unwell.
reason: Paediatric cohort; the finding's claim is about adults and already notes better adolescent prognosis, so this extends (confirms the adolescent subgroup) rather than contradicts. Recovery is self-reported.
